author: cmungall
body: One paper, PMID:12709059 (rat O-MACS/Acsm4), has been curated twice, once correctly by swissprot, the other incorrectly by RGD - **UniProt (Swiss-Prot)** recorded the reactions the paper measured: - RHEA:48340, the general medium-chain fatty acid reaction (EC 6.2.1.2), plus the hexanoate (RHEA:43740), octanoate (RHEA:33631), decanoate (RHEA:33627) and dodecanoate (RHEA:33623) reactions; - the curated function: "Capable of activating medium-chain fatty acids with a preference for C6-12 fatty acids". These map to GO:0031956 *medium-chain fatty acid-CoA ligase activity* (EXP) and GO:0102391 *decanoate-CoA ligase activity* (IDA), and both rows are already in GOA. - **RGD** annotated the same paper to GO:0004321 *fatty-acyl-CoA synthase activity* (IDA). That term is a different enzyme: the fatty acid synthase reaction, EC 2.3.1.86 (acetyl-CoA + n malonyl-CoA + NADPH → long-chain acyl-CoA). The paper's abstract describes *"an acyl-CoA synthetase activity for fatty acid activation"*, which is the ligase reaction (fatty acid + ATP + CoA → acyl-CoA + AMP + PPi). Synthetase and synthase differ by one letter but name different enzyme classes. The RGD row then seeded a family-wide inference: 1. **PAINT IBD:** PTN001944787, the PTHR43605 root (LUCA), has an IBD to GO:0004321 whose only seed is RGD:727928 (dated 2017-02-28 in the PAINT file). The same node carries the correct IBD to GO:0015645 *fatty acid ligase activity*, seeded by eight ACSM genes. 2. **Propagation** (2026-11-01, UniProt 2026_03 and QuickGO): - 12,328 of the 12,837 UniProtKB entries in PTHR43605 (96%) carry GO:0004321, including 8,209 bacterial entries; - 89 IBA rows (33 taxa) cite PTN001944787; - all seven human ACSMs carry it, and every one is EC 6.2.1.2 in UniProt; - mouse Acsm4 also gets it by ISO and Ensembl IEA from the rat row; - PTHR43605 accounts for about 73% of all UniProtKB entries annotated to GO:0004321. We found this while reviewing *Pseudomonas putida* PP_2213 (Q88KS6), an AMP-forming acyl-CoA synthetase that received GO:0004321 by TreeGrafter. **Requested changes** 1. **RGD:** the Acsm4 IDA to GO:0004321 from PMID:12709059 can be deleted. The correct activity from that paper is already annotated by UniProt (GO:0031956, GO:0102391). We have read only the abstract; the UniProt record is the reaction-level reading of the full text. 2. **PAINT, PTN001944787 (PTHR43605 root):** please retract the IBD to GO:0004321 on this node. Its only seed is the row above, and the node already carries the correct GO:0015645. 3. **Please also check:** the IBD to GO:0006633 *fatty acid biosynthetic process* on the same node. Its seeds are MGI IDAs on mouse Acsm1 and Acsm3 (MGI:2152200, MGI:99538) from PMID:11470804. That abstract says *"acyl-CoAs produced by MACS1 and Sa protein are utilized mainly for oxidation"*, so GO:0046949 fatty-acyl-CoA biosynthetic process may have been intended. We have not read the full text. Even if the seeds hold, a LUCA placement is broad. In the prokaryotic subfamily SF10 the term may be right for MbcS-like members (*S. aureus* MbcS supplies branched-chain primers for fatty acid synthesis, PMID:36806679), but not for the archaeal 4-hydroxybutyrate-CoA ligase (*M. sedula* Msed_0406), which works in a CO2-fixation cycle. **Other GO:0004321 rows that may have the same problem (not checked)** Experimental rows on proteins named as acyl-CoA synthetases or acyl-activating enzymes; some may be correct: - MGI: Slc27a3 (IMP, PMID:15469937), propagated to rat by ISO - GeneDB: *T. brucei* Tb09.160.2770/2780/2810/2840 and *Leishmania* ACS1–4 (IDA, PMID:11535136) - TAIR: 4CLL7, 4CLL9 (IDA, PMID:15677481) - MTBBASE: fadD13 (PMID:20027301), fadD28 (PMID:9098059) (IDA) **A note on the term itself (no action requested here)** GO:0004321 follows EC 2.3.1.86. Its accepted IUBMB name is "fatty-acyl-CoA synthase system", with "yeast fatty acid synthase" as an alternative name. It is the fungal two-subunit FAS that releases acyl-CoA; the animal enzyme is EC 2.3.1.85, which maps to GO:0004312 *fatty acid synthase activity*. So the term should only ever apply to fungal FAS subunits, and its label is one letter from "fatty acyl-CoA synthetase". We may raise label and definition questions on go-ontology separately (see go-ontology#8102 for earlier discussion of this term). **Details** Reviews with structured source-defect records (ai-gene-review, branch `claude/lucid-brahmagupta-ep1gba`): - Family review: https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/blob/claude/lucid-brahmagupta-ep1gba/interpro/panther/PTHR43605/PTHR43605-review.yaml - Rat Acsm4: https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/blob/claude/lucid-brahmagupta-ep1gba/genes/rat/Acsm4/Acsm4-ai-review.yaml - Mouse Acsm4: https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/blob/claude/lucid-brahmagupta-ep1gba/genes/mouse/Acsm4/Acsm4-ai-review.yaml - Human ACSM4: https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/blob/claude/lucid-brahmagupta-ep1gba/genes/human/ACSM4/ACSM4-ai-review.yaml - *P. putida* PP_2213: https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/blob/claude/lucid-brahmagupta-ep1gba/genes/PSEPK/PP_2213/PP_2213-ai-review.yaml - *M. sedula* Msed_0406: https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/blob/claude/lucid-brahmagupta-ep1gba/genes/METS5/Msed_0406/Msed_0406-ai-review.yaml - *B. subtilis* YtcI: https://github.com/ai4curation/ai-gene-review/blob/claude/lucid-brahmagupta-ep1gba/genes/BACSU/ytcI/ytcI-ai-review.yaml PAINT rows (PTHR43605-paint.tsv): ``` PTHR43605 PTN001944787 GO:0004321 F IBD RGD:727928 20170228 PTHR43605 PTN001944787 GO:0015645 F IBD MGI:MGI:2152200|MGI:MGI:99538|RGD:727928|UniProtKB:Q08AH1|UniProtKB:Q08AH3|UniProtKB:Q53FZ2|UniProtKB:Q68CK6|UniProtKB:Q9BEA2 20260530 PTHR43605 PTN001944787 GO:0006633 P IBD MGI:MGI:2152200|MGI:MGI:99538 20170228 ```
title: PAINT issue: Retract IBD to GO:0004321 fatty-acyl-CoA synthase on PTN001944787 (PTHR43605 root): one Acsm4 IDA propagated to ~12,000 acyl-CoA synthetases
